stem.en: A drop of water falls on a black sketch-pen line. Rings of yellow, pink and blue appear at the edge of the wet patch. The same water on clean paper shows no colour. What does this show?

text.en: The water made the colours, because water can split white light into colours.
The colours were in the paper, and the water brought them out.
Black ink is a mixture of dyes, and the water spread them apart.
Light bends in the thin wet layer, so the colours are not really there.

explanation.en: The ink holds several dyes, and water carried them out to different distances. The test on clean paper settles it: the same water and the same paper gave no colour, so neither the water nor the paper can be the source. A rainbow in a wet film is a real effect, which makes the light idea reasonable, but these colours stay on the paper after it dries.

hints.en: What was different between the clean patch and the patch on the line?
If the clean paper shows no colour, where must the colours have come from?
